plan.notes: Source: official EECS department 'EECS and ECE B.S. Sample Study Plans' page (https://eecs.berkeley.edu/resources/undergrads/eecs-2/study-plans/), the 4-year sample for students entering with the Math 51/52 calculus sequence complete (track verified 2026-09-30; page last modified 2026-05-28 per site metadata). Catalog year: 2026-2027. How transcribed: the department's term-by-term sample plan was transcribed row-for-row from the published table; course titles and codes use the official Berkeley catalog codes (COMPSCI/ELENG/MATH/PHYSICS). Unit values: every core course carries its official unit value from the 2026-2027 undergraduate guide curriculum table (engineering.berkeley.edu; e.g. COMPSCI 61A/61C, ELENG 64/66, MATH 53/54, COMPSCI 70 = 4) and physics.berkeley.edu (PHYSICS 7A/7B = 4, 5A/5B = 3, 5BL = 2, 89 = 4). Caveats: (1) The department publishes three math-start tracks ('No College Level Math', 'Math 51 Complete', 'Math 51 + 52 Complete'); this plan is the 'Math 51 + 52 Complete' track, the most common for incoming EECS students with AP calculus credit. (2) Generic category rows (H/SS, free electives, ethics, breadth, design, technical electives, probability) are represented as student-choice slots with planning-unit values (4 unless noted); actual units vary by the course chosen. (3) Prereq lists are left empty: the official sample plan does not publish them and the department instructs students to take prerequisite chains in the right order and see an advisor for degree checks. (4) CS 10 is an optional preparatory course for students with minimal programming experience and may be taken before CS 61A; it is not required. (5) College of Engineering minimum is 120 units; this sample sums to exactly 120, matching the page's stated 30-units-per-year average.
